item.title: The Baumol Effect and Jevons paradox are related
item.description:
📝 Each of these phenomena have a name: there’s Jevons Paradox, which means, “We’ll spend more on what gets more productive”, and there’s the Baumol Effect, which means, “We’ll spend more on what doesn’t get more productive. Other goods and services, where AI has relatively less impact, will become more expensive - and we’ll consume more of them anyway. It’s with the blue lines: where are things getting cheaper, in ways that create more jobs, more opportunity, and more spending.
🔗 Read more: https://www.a16z.news/p/why-ac-is-cheap-but-ac-repair-is

item.title: Reselling tickets for profit to be outlawed in UK government crackdown
item.description:
📝 However, the Guardian understands that touts – and ordinary consumers – will no longer be able to charge anything more than the price at which they purchased the ticket in the first place. Resale platforms will be allowed to charge fees on top of that price. Anyone reselling a ticket will also be prohibited from offering more tickets than they could have procured under limits set by the original box office company.
🔗 Read more: https://www.theguardian.com/money/2025/nov/17/reselling-tickets-for-profit-to-be-outlawed-in-uk-government-crackdown

item.title: You can now buy used Ford vehicles on Amazon
item.description:
📝 Ford is the second brand, after Hyundai, to list its vehicles on Amazon’s new car buying site. Starting today, customers can browse, finance, and purchase certified pre-owned Ford vehicles online through Amazon Autos, with in-person pickup at a local Ford dealership. Ford is the second brand name, after Hyundai, to list its vehicles on the site.
🔗 Read more: https://www.theverge.com/news/821258/ford-amazon-auto-online-sales-certified-preowned
